_about: Every gate a command can require, named by what it means. DECISIONS ('gates') are Paul's, set only by scripts/approve.py through his /approve; 'met' means Approved or Approved with Conditions and the files recorded with THAT approval are unchanged (an edit voids only that decision; later ones are flagged 'upstream change'). CONDITIONS are facts the scripts check themselves and log in log.md the first time they are met; nobody approves them. Each decision names its artifact (the status.json mark listing the files the approval covers) and its producer (the command that writes them). R3 (Paul, 2026-10-08): two approvals for discovery + audit. Approval 1 = entity_approved + proof_sheet_approved in one /approve line ('with' names the decision approved in the same line); Approval 2 = audit_approved on its own as soon as the audit is done (D3, Rewrite 4 Phase 3, 2026-10-20: the URL decisions, safe fixes and the blocker handoff no longer wait for the client), then brand_guide_approved when the client's facts are reconciled. discovery_signed_off and blockers_cleared are conditions. page_specs_approved is a global condition Paul meets once with /approve global specs.

_steps_about: Every command step: the gates run.py start checks (looked up here — nowhere else), what it must produce before run.py finish will close it, and (reads) the only files the agent reads for that step (run.py start prints them). {batch} and {page} come from --batch / --page; {prev_post} is the newest blog post. produces: an artifact name (a status.py mark recorded during the run), 'steps:S01,S02' (an outcome for each audit step), 'batch:{batch}:<stage>' (the batch files recorded), 'blog_post' (a new post registered with its file), 'batch_state:{batch}:a|b' (the batch reached one of those states). 'marked:<artifact>' as a gate = that artifact is recorded (status.py mark). In produces, 'a|b' = either artifact recorded by this run.

_modes_about: CM-044. Every producing stage has a mode: review (the /next loop stops after the stage so Paul can look) or auto (the loop goes straight on). Default review. A stage can switch to auto only after it has passed the pilot ('pilot' below; none = always review), only by Paul with /approve <slug>|global mode:<stage>=auto, recorded in status.json and log.md. Decisions (/approve gates) are never stages here and can never be auto.

pilot._about: CM-061 part 6 (rewrite 3 §9): a pilot (1 service + 1 location, briefs and drafts, one approval) runs only for a client's first section, a new industry, or the first section after a change to the specs or the writing rules (methodology/specs/*.md, writing-commercial.md, location-faq.md — the fingerprint each drafts approval records). Otherwise all pages of a section are drafted in one run. status.py pilot <slug> prints the decision and the reason; status.py plan refuses a plan without a pilot when one is needed. 'always' = the old rule. Rewrite 4 (Paul, 2026-10-20): no pilot, even for a client's first section, once the last 3 clients' pilots had no corrections (status.py pilot-corrections --none) at today's writing fingerprint.

_stages_about: R1/R2 (Paul, 2026-10-08). Every step belongs to one stage. A stage runs in its own session on the session model (Haiku — it orchestrates /next, relays agent summaries, prints /approve lines); judgment lives in the agents, whose model is fixed in .claude/agents/<name>.md frontmatter (opus or haiku only). run.py start refuses a step of a new stage in a session that already finished a different stage. 'per_batch' stages are one session per batch. 'any_stage' steps are bookkeeping that may run in any session. A system/design session (editing seo-ops itself) runs on Opus and starts no runs.

_models_about: Rewrite 2 §4 (Q12): the model for each job. Opus where the judgment is hard to check, Sonnet for structured assembly, research and extraction, Haiku for orchestration (the stage chat); mechanics are scripts, no agent (Rewrite 4 Phase 1). Every stage session runs on Haiku. The agent's frontmatter model must match its role here (tests check it); a role marked 'override' passes the model to the Agent call. Paul changes a role only with /approve global model:<step>=<model> (recorded in config.json model_overrides).
